chapter: Will Marion Cook and the Southern Syncopated Orchestra
title: The Southern Syncopated Orchestra: size, format and US tour
summary: The orchestra opened in early 1919 and toured US concert halls with about fifty performers, choirs, quartets and soloists in a mixed concert program with a few ragtime numbers.

blocks.x: Right. And then when did you go with the Southern Syncopators?
The Southern Syncopators? I remember, that we opened in Hagerstown, Maryland, after Christmas, and It was in '19. Yes, that was around February.
February 1919?
February 1919. Then we went on tour. He was taking us to Chicago, where we met Sidney Bechet.
Well, okay, so how big was that orchestra, then?
We had about fifty persons.
Fifty people?
Briggs
Yes, yes. We had double-quartets, choirs, and prima donnas. We had two prima donnas. And the orchestra was just -- did you see -- did you read --
I saw some of this but we have to get it on the tape. So there would have been about -- while you were playing --
What?
You weren't playing theaters, you were playing nightclubs.
No, we didn't play nightclubs. We just played concerts, that's all.
This orchestra was a syncopated orchestra. We went on tour playing concerts for halls, you see.
I see.
In America.
And there would be a stage set, would there, I mean?--
Briggs
A stage, yes.
And would there be backdrops or something?
No, no, just a --
Fake --
What you call a concert hall.
Right.
Like Carnegie Hall, a concert hall.
I see, right.
And we didn't play theaters, it was just concert halls. What you call a concert show.
Right.
You had choirs and double-quartets, quartets, individuals.
It was a mix, a mixed program.
A mixed program, yes.
And a lot of it -- I guess you played a lot of ragtime if they
